adverse_media.summary: The company entered administration along with Greensill Capital Management Company (UK) Ltd. The group collapsed with combined liabilities of more than £1.6bn (as_of March 2021). Credit Suisse had frozen about $10bn of Greensill-linked supply chain finance funds on 2021-03-01. Administrator Grant Thornton reported that GFG Alliance still owed about $587m (as_of April 2026).

The Serious Fraud Office opened an investigation into suspected fraud, fraudulent trading and money laundering at GFG Alliance (Sanjeev Gupta) companies. Its scope includes their financing arrangements with Greensill Capital UK Ltd.
adverse_media.status: Open. I could not confirm whether charges have been brought: the SFO case page did not load.

adverse_media.summary: Lex Greensill (PSC, former director) signed a 9-year UK director disqualification undertaking, effective 2026-06-23 to June 2035. It covers his conduct as director of Greensill Capital (UK) Ltd, including Katerra transactions in late 2020 that removed protections for a Credit Suisse SCF fund investment without the required consents. It also covers causing or allowing the company to use $440m received in November 2020 for purposes other than redeeming fund notes, which led to a $440m loss. The undertaking ended proceedings before the trial due 2026-06-08.

The administrators (Grant Thornton) filed a High Court (Business List) claim for breach of fiduciary duty against former directors Lex Greensill, Sean Hanafin, Divya Eapen, Alastair Eadie, Neil Garrod, Jonathan Lane and Bartholomeus Ras.

Former auditor Saffery (Saffery Champness, auditor 2014–2019) paid £71m to the administrators to settle a claim. Reports describe it as centred on the 2019 audit of Greensill Capital (UK) Ltd. A Financial Reporting Council investigation into the auditor remains ongoing.

Former PM David Cameron, an unpaid Greensill adviser from 2018, lobbied ministers for Greensill's access to COVID loans, and the PM ordered an inquiry. In June 2021 it emerged that the British Business Bank had lent Greensill up to $400m without detailed checks, and the money was passed to Gupta-linked companies, with a potential taxpayer loss of £335m.

output.risk_rationale: Greensill Capital (UK) Limited (08126173) has been in administration since 8 March 2021 after a group collapse with more than £1.6bn of liabilities. It has no active directors, its accounts have been overdue since 2021 and its LEI has lapsed (as_of 2026-11-10). Its sole PSC, Lex Greensill, is on a 9-year UK director disqualification (effective 23 June 2026) for conduct at this company, including the misuse of $440m that should have repaid a Credit Suisse fund. The company is named in an SFO fraud and money-laundering investigation into GFG Alliance financing, opened in May 2021, and I found no confirmed outcome. The administrators are suing seven former directors for breach of fiduciary duty and recovered £71m from the former auditor. The 2021 lobbying and British Business Bank loan controversies add reputational risk. No sanctions matches (OFAC, OFSI, EU) were found for the entity or its PSC, and no director or owner is a PEP. David Cameron, a PEP, was only an adviser. Even so, the insolvency, the enforcement record and the open fraud inquiry make this a high risk.
